_about: Published RAMP-CNN schedule, from the reference implementation Xiangyu-Gao/Radar-multiple-perspective-object-detection (config.py). Kept SEPARATE from RAMP_CNN_train_config.json so the repo default is untouched; select with `--config-variant _reference`. ALREADY MATCHING and carried over from the repo default: lr 1e-5, win_size 16, train/test stride 8, peak_thres 0.2, ols_thres 0.2, max_dets 20, and the three loss terms (_neg_loss, Cont_Loss, balance_cof=4), which the Phase 1 audit found to be faithful ports line for line.
_incomplete: THIS CONFIG IS NOT YET RUNNABLE AS A FAITHFUL REPRODUCTION -- the train/val/test split is still unknown (see _split_gap). Everything else below is the reference's. Running it with a made-up split produces a number that cannot be compared to the published 81.23/84.25.
_scheduler_note: The reference runs CyclicLR(base_lr=1e-6, max_lr=1e-5, step_size_up=430, step_size_down=430) with IS_Steplr=False. CyclicLR is a per-BATCH schedule by construction -- step_size_up counts optimizer steps, not epochs -- so train()'s `cyclic` type steps it per iteration, alongside OneCycleLR. Note cycle_momentum is forced False: it defaults True and then requires a 'momentum' key in the optimizer's param_groups, which Adam does not have (torch raises ValueError at construction). Verified: lr rises 1e-6 -> 1e-5 over steps 0-430, falls back by 860, peaks again at 1290. Until 2026-09-02 this pair had no cyclic support and RAMP_CNN_train_config.json used StepLR(10, 0.9) as a stand-in, which decays monotonically instead of oscillating; the reference's own StepLR branch, unused here, decays with gamma 0.1 rather than 0.9.
_split_gap: UNRESOLVED. `dataloader.split_sequence` below is left EMPTY deliberately -- fill in the paper's sequence split before treating any run from this config as a reproduction. (Note resolve_configs only strips `_`-prefixed keys at the TOP level, so notes cannot live inside the dataloader block.) Phase 0 recorded published scores and eval protocols but not data splits, and the RAMP-CNN paper's train/test division of the 22 UWCR sequences is not in this repo. The Phase 1 result (mAP 0.9295) used a 3-sequence smoke split with a SINGLE validation sequence -- mAR reached 1.0000 at several epochs, so it was probably an easy one -- and is not comparable to the published 81.23/84.25, which is the full dataset. Recovering the split needs the reference repo, which is not checked out locally. Leaving `split_sequence` empty here rather than inventing one.
_metrics_note: AP/AR with a SIZE-ADAPTIVE DISTANCE threshold and CFAR peak extraction at 0.2 -- not IoU. Published per scene: ParkingLot 97.38/98.37, Curbside 79.25/84.21, On-road 57.07/64.85, overall 81.23/84.25 (Table III). Nighttime data is test-only and is NOT scored numerically in the paper, so any overall figure that includes it is not comparable. RAMP_CNN_evaluation returns mAP and mAR; its mIoU is structurally absent, not collapsed.
_metric_is_a_threshold_note: detect_peaks requires a strict local maximum in a 3x5 window, so mAP stays at EXACTLY 0 until the predicted confmap sharpens past that bar, then rises steeply: 0.0000 through epoch 7, 0.1833 at 8, ~0.15 at 10-11, 0.5761 at 12, 0.9103 at 13, 0.9295 at 19. Every attempt before Phase 1 ran 6 epochs, entirely inside the flat region. A zero from a short run means 'not yet', never 'broken' -- do not stop this pair early on a zero.
_batch_size_note: batch 3, the reference's, not the repo default's 4. Unlike RADDet this is not tied to a step-counted schedule threshold, but step_size_up=430 IS counted in optimizer steps, so the batch size determines how many epochs one half-cycle spans.
